description:
Found by fz-5xp.55's fixture, which failed on `run` while passing on `interp`.

    fnp walk(<<_c, rest :: binary>>, n), do: walk(rest, n + 1)
    fnp walk(_b, n), do: n

    64 bytes: interp=64  run=64
    65 bytes: interp=65  run=0     <-- silently no match
   160 bytes: interp=160 run=0

The bisect lands exactly on SHARED_BIN_THRESHOLD_BYTES. Above it a binary is
held as a PROCBIN rather than a BITSTRING, and:

    RuntimeTestAxis::Binaries => e.kind_flag(value, ValueKind::BITSTRING)

asks about one representation. A PROCBIN answers NO to the Binaries axis, and
RuntimeTestAxis::of_value maps PROCBIN to no axis at all, so it answers no to
EVERY runtime type test. The bitstring region test is never even reached --
fz_bs_reader_init is not called.

Both a clause head and a `case` are affected. It is silent: the value falls to
the next clause.

THE SHAPE, AGAIN (fz-5xp.21). One question -- 'is this a binary' -- with three
implementations: procbin::is_bitstring_like (right, both tags),
emit_bitstring_like_guard in native_codegen/receive.rs (right, both tags), and
these two (wrong, one tag).

FIX: ValueKind::BINARY_REPRS names the representations once; of_value,
matches_runtime_axis and the native emit_axis all ask it. A third
representation would then reach every door by construction.
title: A binary over 64 bytes matches NO bitstring pattern on the native doors
